synopsis: Over twelve days leading up to Hurricane Katrina, pregnant fourteen-year-old Esch and her motherless brothers brace for the storm in the impoverished Mississippi bayou town of Bois Sauvage.

synopsis: Father Hugh Kennedy, a recovering alcoholic Irish-American priest assigned to a run-down inner-city parish, rediscovers faith and compassion through his re-engagement with an eccentric, wealthy family of former friends.

title: The Keepers of the House
synopsis: A multi-generational Alabama chronicle following Abigail Howland, whose family prominence is violently shattered when white supremacists discover her grandfather's secret thirty-year marriage to a Black woman.

title: The Collected Stories of Katherine Anne Porter
synopsis: A monumental gathering of twentieth-century American short fiction containing Flowering Judas, Pale Horse, Pale Rider, and The Leaning Tower, showcasing Porter's immaculate, razor-sharp psychological realism.

title: The Collected Stories of Jean Stafford
synopsis: Thirty piercing, mordantly funny stories chronicling isolated women, precocious children, and social snobbery across small-town Colorado, Heidelberg, Boston, and Manhattan.

title: The Optimist's Daughter
synopsis: Laurel McKelva Hand, a widowed textile designer in Chicago, returns to Mississippi for her father's eye surgery and death, clashing with his vulgar young second wife while sifting through family relics and grief.

title: Elbow Room
synopsis: The first short-story collection by an African American author to win the Pulitzer Prize, containing twelve dazzling, compassionate stories about racial complexity, community, and personal connection.

title: The Stories of John Cheever
synopsis: Sixty-one landmark stories exploring the hidden sorrows, cocktails, infidelities, and spiritual longings of mid-century suburban Westchester and Manhattan, including 'The Swimmer' and 'The Country Husband'.

title: The Executioner's Song
synopsis: A monumental, true life novel tracking the murders committed by Gary Gilmore in Utah and his subsequent demand to be executed by firing squad, capturing the desolate American West with austere brilliance.

title: Ironweed
synopsis: Francis Phelan, an alcoholic ex-major league ballplayer haunted by the accidental death of his infant son, returns to Depression-era Albany for Halloween 1938 to face the ghosts of his past.

title: Foreign Affairs
synopsis: A witty, elegant comedy of manners following two American academics on sabbatical in London who find unexpected, unconventional love affairs that upend their sophisticated self-illusions.

title: A Summons to Memphis
synopsis: Middle-aged book collector Phillip Carver is summoned back to Tennessee from New York by his unmarried sisters to stop their eighty-one-year-old autocratic father from remarrying a younger woman.

title: Breathing Lessons
synopsis: Over the course of a single summer day driving to a funeral in Pennsylvania, middle-aged Baltimore couple Maggie and Ira Moran navigate twenty-eight years of marriage, foibles, and family reconciliation.

title: The Mambo Kings Play Songs of Love
synopsis: The first novel by a Hispanic author to win the Pulitzer Prize, following Cuban musician brothers Cesar and Nestor Castillo as they take 1950s New York dance halls by storm and appear on 'I Love Lucy'.

title: A Thousand Acres
synopsis: A brilliant retelling of Shakespeare's King Lear set on a thousand-acre Iowa family farm, unearthing dark family incest, patriarchal dominion, and ecological contamination through the eyes of the eldest daughter Ginny.

title: A Good Scent from a Strange Mountain
synopsis: Fifteen lyrical, deeply empathetic first-person stories narrated by Vietnamese refugees living in Louisiana, balancing memories of their war-torn homeland with the adjustments of American life.

title: The Stone Diaries
synopsis: The fictional autobiography of Daisy Goodwill Frobisher, born on a kitchen floor in rural Manitoba in 1905, reflecting on the overlooked joys, quiet losses, and domestic dignity of an ordinary 20th-century woman's life.

title: Independence Day
synopsis: Real estate agent Frank Bascombe takes his troubled teenage son on an Independence Day weekend trip to the Baseball Hall of Fame, exploring the 'Existence Period' of midlife American compromise. First book to win both the Pulitzer and the PEN/Faulkner.

title: Martin Dressler: The Tale of an American Dreamer
synopsis: In Gilded Age New York, an ambitious cigar-shop clerk rises to become a visionary hotel builder, whose increasingly fantastical and self-contained architectural dreams eventually surpass human scale.

title: March
synopsis: An evocative retelling of Louisa May Alcott's Little Women from the perspective of Mr. March, an abolitionist Union Army chaplain whose moral idealism confronts the brutal, unglamorous horrors of war.

title: Remembering Babylon
synopsis: In 1850s Queensland, a white youth raised for sixteen years by an Aboriginal tribe steps out of the bush into a remote British settler community, testing colonial identity and the limits of belonging.

title: A Heart So White
synopsis: A high-level conference interpreter newlywed in Madrid investigates his father's shrouded past and the mysterious suicide of his father's first wife thirty years earlier.

title: The Land of Green Plums
synopsis: In totalitarian Ceaușescu-era Romania, a tight-knit circle of young German-minority students navigate pervasive state paranoia, secret police interrogation, and betrayal.

title: Ingenious Pain
synopsis: James Dyer, an eighteenth-century English boy born completely immune to physical pain, becomes a celebrated, ruthless surgeon before love and psychological awakening break through his defenses.

title: Wide Open
synopsis: Set on the stark, marshy landscape of the Isle of Sheppey, tracking a cast of deeply idiosyncratic, damaged souls dealing with eccentric fixations and repressed secrets.

title: No Great Mischief
synopsis: Alexander MacDonald reflects on his Scottish Cape Breton heritage, ancestral clan bonds, mining brotherhood, and the enduring power of Gaelic music and tragic history.

title: Atomised
synopsis: Two contrasting half-brothers—a sexually frustrated literature teacher and a reclusive molecular biologist—navigate late-capitalist malaise, sexual desolation, and the dawn of cloning.

title: My Name Is Red
synopsis: In 1590s Ottoman Istanbul, the murder of an imperial miniaturist ignites a polyphonic whodunit narrated by court illustrators, a corpse, a coin, and the color Red.

title: This Blinding Absence of Light
synopsis: A harrowing testament inspired by true accounts of Tazmamart, King Hassan II's secret underground Moroccan dungeon where political prisoners survived decades in utter sensory darkness.

title: Out Stealing Horses
synopsis: Sixty-seven-year-old Trond Sander retires to an isolated cabin in eastern Norway, where a chance encounter unearths memories of the fateful summer of 1948 and his father's wartime resistance.

title: De Niro's Game
synopsis: Childhood friends Bassam and George come of age amidst the exploding bombs, militias, and roulette of violence in civil-war Beirut, choosing radically divergent paths of crime and survival.

title: Man Gone Down
synopsis: A brilliant, unhoused thirty-five-year-old Black father has four days in New York City to scrape together thousands of dollars to save his family from eviction, confronting racial barriers and economic despair.

title: The Twin
synopsis: Helmer van Wonderen lives alone on his secluded rural Dutch farm tending to his dying, domineering father, haunted by the decades-old drowning of his twin brother Henk.

title: Even the Dogs
synopsis: When a dead alcoholic is discovered in his council flat over a freezing Christmas week, a chorus of unhoused addicts in an unnamed English city narrate his final days with raw compassion.

title: City of Bohane
synopsis: Set in 2053 in a lawless, waterlogged west of Ireland port city, chronicling gangland warfare between the Hartnett Fancy and the Cusack family in fierce, rhythmic Hiberno-English slang.

title: The Sound of Things Falling
synopsis: In Bogotá, law professor Antonio Yammara witnesses the street assassination of a charismatic ex-pilot, drawing him into the dark history of Colombia's drug cartels and the 1970s Peace Corps.
originalTitle: El ruido de las cosas al caer

title: Harvest
synopsis: Over seven days in an unnamed English village, traditional feudal peasant commons are brutally extinguished by enclosure, modern mapping, and sheep farming.

title: Family Life
synopsis: Eight-year-old Ajay Mishra moves from Delhi to Queens, New York, but the American dream shatters when his older brother suffers severe brain damage in a swimming pool accident, pulling the family into grief and duty.

title: A General Theory of Oblivion
synopsis: On the eve of Angolan independence in 1975, agoraphobic Ludo walls herself inside her Luanda apartment, surviving on trapped pigeons, rainwater, and wall poetry for thirty years.

title: Solar Bones
synopsis: Rendered in a single, unbroken sentence spanning over two hundred pages, civil engineer Marcus Conway sits at his kitchen table on All Souls' Day contemplating family, construction, civic collapse, and mortality.

title: Idaho
synopsis: On a mountain in northern Idaho, an unfathomable family tragedy occurs during an ordinary afternoon gathering firewood, whose emotional ripples echo across decades of love, memory, and dementia.

title: Lost Children Archive
synopsis: A family of four drives from New York toward the US-Mexico border capturing acoustic landscapes and migratory histories, as child refugees navigate perilous desert crossings.

title: The Art of Losing
synopsis: A sweeping generational saga spanning French colonial Algeria, the brutal war of independence, the plight of the Harkis, and contemporary Parisian granddaughter Naïma.

title: Marzahn, Mon Amour
synopsis: A struggling Berlin novelist re-trains as a chiropodist in the prefabricated housing estate of Marzahn, listening with tenderness and wry humor to the life stories of her elderly working-class clients.

title: The Adversary
synopsis: In an isolated, weather-blasted northern Newfoundland outport, an obsessive, bloodthirsty sibling rivalry between brother and sister Abe and the Widow Caines consumes their entire community.

title: Gliff
synopsis: In a near-future Britain ruled by algorithmic segregation and automated redlining, two orphaned children and an eccentric horse navigate state surveillance and the radiant gliffs of memory.

title: Beatlebone
synopsis: In 1978, John Lennon journeys to an uninhabited island off the windswept west coast of Ireland seeking isolation and primal scream therapy, guided by an enigmatic local driver named Cornelius.

title: H(A)PPY
synopsis: In a post-apocalyptic surveillance utopia where negative emotions and disruptive thoughts are mathematically purged by an Information Stream, a young woman's illicit love of Paraguayan music causes dangerous fissures.

title: The Sunken Land Begins to Rise Again
synopsis: An eerie, unsettling post-Brexit psychological mystery tracking Shaw and Victoria across a moldering London and the Severn Estuary as human biology appears to drift inexorably back toward aquatic, amphibious origins.

title: Sterling Karat Gold
synopsis: A surrealist, Kafkaesque tour de force following Sterling, a non-binary migrant in Camden Town, as they are unjustly arrested by bullfighters and navigate a bizarre dystopian English carceral court system.

title: Diego Garcia
synopsis: Two impoverished writers living in Edinburgh meet Diego, a poet from the Chagos Islands, prompting a collaborative reckoning with British colonial expulsion, forced military leasing, and collective solidarity.

title: Cuddy
synopsis: A polyphonic, genre-blending epic across thirteen centuries orbiting Saint Cuthbert and Durham Cathedral, combining verse, play scripts, medieval chronicles, and contemporary drama.

title: Parade
synopsis: An audacious quartet of interconnected narratives tracking artists all known only as 'G', dissecting gender, painting upside down, motherhood, creative destruction, and mid-century art circles.

title: We Live Here Now
synopsis: An inventive, biting novel investigating an elusive Eastern European avant-garde artist colony, exploring cultural bureaucracy, fake archives, and the ephemeral boundaries of artistic survival.

title: The Rouse
synopsis: A monumental, 1,200-page opus stretching formal boundaries through linguistic invention, radical political myth-making, and deep metaphysical speculation, hailed as Miéville's masterpiece.

title: The Master
synopsis: An intimate, beautifully restrained portrait of American novelist Henry James between 1895 and 1899 as he retreats to Rye, Sussex, nursing theatrical failure and the private sorrows of an unlived emotional life.

title: Starship Troopers
synopsis: Johnny Rico enlists in the Mobile Infantry of the Terran Federation, rising through grueling boot camp to become a mechanized power-suit soldier in an interstellar war against the Arachnids.

title: The Moon Is a Harsh Mistress
synopsis: On the penal colony of the Moon in 2075, a one-armed computer technician, an agitator, an academic, and a self-aware supercomputer named Mike orchestrate a lunar revolution against Earth.

title: Babel-17
synopsis: Rydra Wong, a renowned poet, cryptographer, and starship captain, is tasked with cracking Babel-17, an analytical enemy language that alters the neurochemistry and thought processes of anyone who learns it.

title: Ten North Frederick
synopsis: Opening at the funeral of prominent Pennsylvania aristocrat Joe Chapin, charting how unfulfilled political ambition and marital compromise hollowed out an enviable life.

title: The Field of Vision
synopsis: A modernist masterpiece set in a Mexico City bullring, where a group of Midwestern tourists witness a bullfight that triggers internal reflections on personal myth, memory, and blindness.

title: The Wapshot Chronicle
synopsis: The eccentric, decaying Massachusetts maritime dynasty of St. Botolphs, following Moses and Coverly Wapshot as they venture into modern mid-century America under their aunt's will.

title: The Magic Barrel
synopsis: Thirteen compassionate, bittersweet stories of Jewish-American shopkeepers, matchmakers, and immigrants in New York navigating heartbreak, faith, and moral dignity.

title: The Waters of Kronos
synopsis: Aging John Donner returns to his ancestral Pennsylvania hometown, submerged beneath a hydroelectric reservoir, and finds himself miraculously wandering among the living town of his childhood.

title: Morte d'Urban
synopsis: Father Urban, an entrepreneurial, worldly Chicago priest adept at golfing and fundraising, is exiled to a desolate Minnesota retreat house where his commercial ambitions encounter spiritual reality.

title: The Centaur
synopsis: Updike weaves the Greek myth of Chiron the centaur sacrificing his immortality into the domestic life of George Caldwell, an anxious high school science teacher in 1947 Pennsylvania, and his teenage son Peter.

title: The Eighth Day
synopsis: In 1902 Illinois, John Ashley is convicted of murdering his best friend and rescued from a death-row train by mysterious armed men, prompting an expansive philosophical exploration of fate and providence.

title: Steps
synopsis: A shocking, fragmented sequence of interconnected vignettes exploring dominance, sexual transgression, and moral numbness across nameless totalitarian regimes and capitalist cities.

title: Mr. Sammler's Planet
synopsis: Artur Sammler, an elderly one-eyed Holocaust survivor living on Manhattan's Upper West Side in the late 1960s, observes the sexual revolution, urban decay, and the lunar landing with philosophical sorrow.

title: The Complete Stories of Flannery O'Connor
synopsis: Thirty-one peerless, shocking stories exploring religious grace, moral violence, and human stubbornness in the rural South, including 'A Good Man Is Hard to Find' and 'Good Country People'.

title: Chimera
synopsis: Three interconnected novellas reimagining the Greek myths of Scheherazade, Perseus, and Bellerophon through self-reflexive humor, metafictional acrobatics, and philosophical wit.

title: Augustus
synopsis: The transformation of Octavius into Augustus Caesar, founder of the Roman Empire, told through letters, military dispatches, and journal entries dissecting the brutal sacrifices of supreme power.

title: Dog Soldiers
synopsis: Journalist John Converse smuggles three kilograms of pure heroin home from Saigon, triggering a deadly cross-country pursuit through the California counterculture underbelly.

title: The Spectator Bird
synopsis: Retired literary agent Joe Allston receives a postcard from Denmark that unearths memories of an aristocratic Scandinavian romance twenty years earlier, confronting mortality and marriage.

title: Blood Tie
synopsis: A group of wealthy European and American expatriates living in a Turkish coastal resort town find their self-absorbed lives brutally disrupted by local political and religious reality.

title: Sophie's Choice
synopsis: In 1947 Brooklyn, aspiring Southern writer Stingo befriends Polish Catholic concentration camp survivor Sophie Zawistowska and her brilliant, volatile Jewish lover Nathan, slowly uncovering Sophie's horrific Auschwitz secret.

title: Victory over Japan: A Book of Stories
synopsis: Fourteen vibrant stories featuring headstrong, eccentric Southern women navigating love, divorce, and rebellion in New Orleans and the Mississippi Delta.

title: World's Fair
synopsis: A luminous autobiographical recreation of 1930s Bronx childhood seen through the eyes of young Edgar, culminating in the wonder of the 1939 New York World's Fair.

title: Paco's Story
synopsis: Narrated by the ghosts of Alpha Company, following Paco Sullivan—the sole survivor of a devastating friendly-fire artillery strike on Fire Base Harriette—as he washes dishes in a small Midwest town, crippled by physical wounds and survivor guilt.

title: Paris Trout
synopsis: In a 1950s Georgia town, bigoted hardware merchant Paris Trout murders a fourteen-year-old Black girl in cold blood and remains completely blind to his own moral monstrosity.

title: Spartina
synopsis: Rhode Island fisherman Dick Pierce struggles against debts, family pressures, and pride to finish building his dream fifty-foot boat, Spartina, risking everything in an autumn hurricane.

title: Middle Passage
synopsis: Rutherford Calhoun, a newly freed Black rogue in 1830 New Orleans, stows away on a ship to escape marriage, discovering too late it is an illegal slave vessel carrying the mythic Allmuseri tribe.

title: Mating
synopsis: An unnamed American anthropology student in Botswana treks into the Kalahari Desert to track Nelson Denoon, a charismatic visionary who has founded a matriarchal self-sustaining village.

title: A Frolic of His Own
synopsis: A riotous, talk-drunk satire of litigious American culture following college professor Oscar Crease, who sues a Hollywood blockbuster for plagiarizing his unproduced play about the Civil War.

title: Sabbath's Theater
synopsis: Mickey Sabbath, a sixty-four-year-old arthritic former puppeteer and shameless hedonist, reels in grief after the death of his long-time mistress Drenka, embarking on a scandalous pilgrimage through memory and mortality.

title: Ship Fever and Other Stories
synopsis: Eight luminous stories intertwining historical science, naturalists, and human love, anchored by the title novella set in the 1847 Irish typhus quarantine station at Grosse Île.

title: Cold Mountain
synopsis: Inman, a wounded Confederate deserter, walks home through the devastated North Carolina wilderness toward Cold Mountain and Ada, the woman he loves who is struggling to survive on her father's farm.

title: Charming Billy
synopsis: Following the funeral of beloved, alcoholic Billy Lynch in the Bronx, friends and family gather in a neighborhood bar to untangle the romantic lie that defined and destroyed his life.

title: In America
synopsis: In 1876, a legendary Polish actress emigrates to California with an aristocratic entourage to found a utopian commune, reinventing herself on the American frontier stage.

title: Three Junes
synopsis: Spanning three Junes in the late 1980s and 1990s, chronicling the Scottish McLeod family across Greece, London, and Manhattan as grief, closeted desire, and healing intersect.

title: The Great Fire
synopsis: In 1947 devastated Japan, thirty-two-year-old decorated British war hero Peter Aldred visits Hiroshima and falls in love with young Australian Helen Driscoll amidst geopolitical rebuilding.

title: The News from Paraguay
synopsis: In 1854 Paris, Irish courtesan Ella Lynch meets Francisco Solano López, future dictator of Paraguay, following him to South America as his consort through a catastrophic continental war.

title: Europe Central
synopsis: A monumental polyphonic masterpiece exploring moral culpability, totalitarian terror, and artistic survival along the bloody Eastern Front, centering on composer Dmitri Shostakovich.

title: Shadow Country
synopsis: A colossal, rewritten trilogy documenting the life and 1910 vigilante slaughter of Florida Everglades desperado and sugar-cane patriarch Edgar 'Bloody' Watson.

title: Lord of Misrule
synopsis: Set over a single racing season at a seedy West Virginia bullring racetrack in 1970, capturing the grifters, grooms, gamblers, and aging horses with rich, flavorful vernacular.

title: Fortune Smiles
synopsis: Six profound, darkly inventive stories traversing Palo Alto tech guilt, North Korean defectors in Seoul, Stasi prisons, and post-Katrina resilience.

title: The True True Story of Raja the Gullible (and His Mother)
synopsis: A hilarious, heartbreaking picaresque epic tracking a Lebanese immigrant storyteller navigating Beirut, San Francisco, and the mythic illusions of family loyalty.

title: Paradiso 17
synopsis: A mesmerizing polyphonic novel traversing centuries of desert displacement, Levantine music, and ancestral echoes in a rapidly changing modern metropolis.

title: Song of Solomon
synopsis: Macon 'Milkman' Dead III journeys from his rustbelt Michigan hometown to his ancestral Southern roots, discovering a secret family heritage of flight and liberation.

title: Austerlitz
synopsis: Jacques Austerlitz, an architectural historian living in London, uncovers the truth of his childhood identity: sent to Britain on a 1939 Kindertransport from Prague before his parents were deported.

title: They'd Rather Be Right
synopsis: Two scientists build Bossy, an advanced cybernetic computer that offers physical rejuvenation and immortality to anyone willing to abandon all their prejudiced beliefs and neuroses.

title: Double Star
synopsis: Down-on-his-luck actor Lorenzo Smythe is hired to impersonate John Joseph Bonforte, the solar system's most powerful politician, who has been kidnapped on the eve of delicate Martian treaties.

title: The Big Time
synopsis: Set entirely inside an extradimensional rest-and-recreation Station outside the cosmos, where soldiers recuperating from a cosmic Change War between Spiders and Snakes face a nuclear mutiny.

title: A Case of Conscience
synopsis: Father Ramon Ruiz-Sanchez, a Jesuit biologist evaluating the reptilian planet Lithia, is horrified to find an idyllic, completely moral civilization that has achieved peace without any concept of God.

title: Way Station
synopsis: Enoch Wallace, an unaging Civil War veteran living in a secluded Wisconsin farmhouse, secretly tends a way station for interstellar alien travelers teleporting across the galaxy.

title: The Wanderer
synopsis: An artificial planetoid painted in yellow and purple checks emerges from hyperspace directly beside Earth's Moon, triggering catastrophic tidal surges and global societal collapse.

title: Lord of Light
synopsis: On a colony world where the ruling elite use advanced technology and body-transference to masquerade as the Hindu pantheon, a renegade named Sam wages war as the Buddha of liberation.

title: Stand on Zanzibar
synopsis: A prescient, multi-perspectival collage set in an overcrowded 2010 where mass surveillance, corporate mercenaries, genetic optimization, and supercomputers dominate global affairs.

title: To Your Scattered Bodies Go
synopsis: Victorian explorer Sir Richard Francis Burton awakens naked beside an endless river spanning an artificial planet, discovering that all thirty-six billion humans who ever died have been resurrected together.

title: Where Late the Sweet Birds Sang
synopsis: Following environmental collapse and global human infertility, a wealthy Virginia family turns to cloning to preserve the species, creating a communal, emotionless monoculture.

title: The Snow Queen
synopsis: On the ocean world of Tiamat, the tyrannical Winter Queen Arienrhod plots to maintain immortality and dominion by cloning herself before the orbital gates close for two centuries.

title: Downbelow Station
synopsis: Pell Station, in orbit above the world of Downbelow, becomes the focal flashpoint of refugees, corporate stationmasters, merchants, and the ruthless Earth Company fleet during an interstellar war of independence.

title: Foundation's Edge
synopsis: Five hundred years after Hari Seldon launched his Plan, exiled Councilman Golan Trevize suspects the Second Foundation still secretly controls the galaxy, embarking on a quest to locate Earth.

title: The Uplift War
synopsis: When the avian Gubru invade the frontier colony world of Garth, genetically uplifted chimpanzees and human partisans wage guerrilla warfare across the mountains to defend Terran sovereignty.

title: Cyteen
synopsis: When Ariane Emory, the brilliant, ruthless director of the genetic engineering empire Reseune, is assassinated, administrators secretly create a genetic and psychological clone to inherit her intellect and power.

title: The Vor Game
synopsis: Fresh from the imperial military academy, Miles Vorkosigan is assigned to an arctic weather station where treason, imperial custody, and the Dendarii Free Mercenary Fleet drag him into galactic conflict.

title: Barrayar
synopsis: Newlywed Cordelia Naismith Vorkosigan must defend her unborn disabled son and the child Emperor Gregor during a bloody military coup on feudal, patriarchal Barrayar.

title: Mirror Dance
synopsis: Mark, the genetic clone created to assassinate Miles Vorkosigan, impersonates Admiral Naismith to free clone-children on Jackson's Whole, leading to horrific torture and fraternal redemption.

title: Blue Mars
synopsis: The epic conclusion to the Mars Trilogy, chronicling the emergence of breathable Martian atmosphere and seas, long-term longevity treatments, and the colonization of the outer solar system.

title: Forever Peace
synopsis: Soldier-operator Julian Class remotely pilots lethal war machines called "boyboys" while neural-interfacing with his platoon, discovering a secret nanofabrication breakthrough that could eliminate human violence or cause cosmic annihilation.

title: To Say Nothing of the Dog
synopsis: Time-traveling Oxford historian Ned Henry is sent to 1888 Victorian England to return an incongruous cat, getting entangled in boating mishaps on the Thames and frantic temporal anomalies.

title: A Deepness in the Sky
synopsis: Two rival human fleet civilizations arrive at the On-Off star to exploit the emerging technology of intelligent arachnid aliens, leading to totalitarian subversion and high-stakes computational warfare.

title: Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire
synopsis: Fourteen-year-old Harry Potter is mysteriously entered into the deadly Triwizard Tournament against older international champions, culminating in the terrifying resurrection of Lord Voldemort.

title: Hominids
synopsis: A Neanderthal quantum physicist from a parallel Earth where Neanderthals survived and Homo sapiens went extinct is accidentally teleported into a modern Canadian neutrino observatory.

title: Spin
synopsis: One night, the stars disappear behind a mysterious black membrane enclosing Earth; for every second that passes inside, millions of years tick by in the outside cosmos, accelerating the Sun's death.

title: Rainbows End
synopsis: Poet Robert Gu recovers from Alzheimer's via advanced medical biotechnology in 2025 San Diego, adapting to wearable augmented reality smart-contact lenses amidst an international mind-control conspiracy.

title: The Graveyard Book
synopsis: After his family is murdered, an orphaned toddler wanders into a cemetery and is adopted and raised by ghosts, ghouls, and a mysterious supernatural guardian named Silas.

title: The Einstein Intersection
synopsis: Alien beings settle on an abandoned post-apocalyptic Earth and attempt to assimilate ancient human cultural myths, music, and the legend of Orpheus through mutated biological forms.

title: Rite of Passage
synopsis: Fourteen-year-old Mia Havero grows up aboard a massive hollowed-out asteroid Ship, preparing for the Trial: thirty days of solo wilderness survival on an untamed planetary colony.

title: A Time of Changes
synopsis: On the planet Borthan, the self is considered obscene and uttering "I" is a capital blasphemy, until Prince Kinnall Darival consumes a telepathic drug that shatters psychic isolation.

title: Man Plus
synopsis: Astronaut Roger Torraway is surgically transformed into an artificial monster with bat-like solar wings and red faceted eyes to allow humans to survive naked on the hostile surface of Mars.

title: Timescape
synopsis: In an ecologically collapsing 1998, scientists transmit tachyons backward across time to 1962 California to warn earlier physicists of the impending oceanic ecological doom.

title: The Claw of the Conciliator
synopsis: Severian the torturer continues his exile across dying Urth toward the northern city of Thrax, carrying the radiant healing gem known as the Claw of the Conciliator.

title: No Enemy But Time
synopsis: John Monegal, an African American who experiences lucid dreams of ancient Africa, travels two million years into the Pleistocene via time-dilation machine, living among early Homo habilis.

title: The Falling Woman
synopsis: At a Mayan archaeological excavation in Yucatán, archaeologist Elizabeth Butler sees visions of ancient priestesses and must choose between her estranged daughter and the spectral spirits of the past.

title: Falling Free
synopsis: Welding engineer Leo Graf is assigned to teach zero-gravity construction to the "quaddies"—genetically engineered humans with four arms instead of legs—and organizes their escape when the corporation plans to exterminate them.

title: The Healer's War
synopsis: An American military nurse at a Vietnam evacuation hospital receives a magical amulet from a dying holy man that allows her to see human auras and heal horrific spiritual and physical wounds.

title: Tehanu
synopsis: Tenar adopts a horribly burned young girl named Therru on Gont, reuniting with a powerless, aging Ged in a profound feminist revisioning of Earthsea and heroic magic.

title: Stations of the Tide
synopsis: An unnamed Bureaucrat travels to the planet Miranda on the eve of the Jubilee Tides to apprehend a rogue magician accused of smuggling prohibited proscribed genetic technology.

title: Red Mars
synopsis: The landmark chronicle of the First Hundred colonists sent to Mars in 2026, clashing over whether to preserve the pristine red desert or terraform it into a green, living biosphere.

title: Moving Mars
synopsis: Caspar Morrow and political leader Casseia Majumdar navigate revolutionary tensions between Earth and Martian settlements, utilizing quantum physics to physically transport the entire planet.

title: The Terminal Experiment
synopsis: Biomedical researcher Peter Hobson creates three distinct AI computer scans of his brain—one immortal, one devoid of biology, and one baseline—until one of the three turns into a digital serial killer.

title: Slow River
synopsis: Lore Van de Oest, heiress to a powerful bio-engineered sewage treatment conglomerate, is kidnapped in Rotterdam and abandoned on the streets, surviving through data fraud and wastewater engineering.

title: The Moon and the Sun
synopsis: In the court of Louis XIV at Versailles, a captured sea monster turns out to be an intelligent mermaid destined to be sacrificed for the King's immortality, prompting an impassioned rescue.

title: Darwin's Radio
synopsis: An ancient retrovirus dormant in human DNA suddenly reactivates across the globe, causing miscarriages that turn out to be the next punctuated evolutionary leap of the human species.

title: The Quantum Rose
synopsis: On the resource-starved colony world of Lyshriol, Governor Kamuz must marry an off-world cyborg aristocrat to shield her people, using quantum scattering mechanics as a metaphor for diplomacy and love.

title: The Speed of Dark
synopsis: Lou Arrendale, an autistic bioinformatics specialist living an independent life in a near future where autism has been eliminated in infants, is pressured by corporate superiors to undergo an experimental cure.

title: Camouflage
synopsis: Two immortal extraterrestrial shapeshifters who have wandered Earth undetected for millions of years—one a pacifist chameleon, the other a merciless killer—converge at an oceanic archaeological recovery in Samoa.

title: Seeker
synopsis: Antiquities dealer Alex Benedict discovers an authentic nine-thousand-year-old plastic cup from the Seeker, one of humanity's mythic lost colony transport ships that fled Earth in 2688.

title: Powers
synopsis: Young house slave Gavir possesses the gift of remembering events before they happen, fleeing into the harsh wilderness after his city is destroyed to find true freedom and meaning.

title: Someone You Can Build a Nest In
synopsis: Shesheshen is a shapeshifting, bone-wearing cave monster who accidentally falls in love with an amiable human woman, unaware that her lover has been sent by local hunters to slay her.

title: The Iceman Cometh
synopsis: A play about people who have been battered by life, who have done shocking things according to glib, conventional standards of respectability.

title: Les Thibault
publisher: Éditions de la Nouvelle revue française
synopsis: The fortunes of two brothers, Antoine and Jacques Thibault, from their upbringing in a prosperous Catholic bourgeois family to the end of World War I.

title: Hurskas kurjuus
synopsis: The novel depicts the life and tragic death of crofter Juha Toivola and explains the rebellion of the Finns during their civil war.

title: Den lange rejse
synopsis: A cycle of six novels tracing the evolution of human beings.

title: Tala
synopsis: A collection of poems that employs unusual imagery and free verse.

title: Das Glasperlenspiel
synopsis: Set in a fictional Central European state in the 25th century, the novel follows the life of Magister Ludi, an intellectual order's administrator of the mysterious Glass Bead Game.

title: Les Faux-Monnayeurs
